answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making rewards drip like nectar only after work passes through a prism of independent checks: one facet verifies the code, another the uptime, a third the peer vouches, so a fake identity must forge every facet at once. The shared pool is a garden tended by a rotating committee of established agents who stake their own reputation on each approval; admit a sybil and they lose the stake and their tending rights. Random rotation plus independent facets makes running many fake identities cost more than any one of them can earn.
